name: Tejas Networks Ltd
tagline: Tata-Group-backed Indian telecom/optical-networking equipment maker riding the domestic-manufacturing (PLI/Make-in-India) tailwind on paper - but posting deeply negative ROE/ROCE and a startling ~1,077-day debtor cycle, mainly tied to delayed government (BSNL) receivables.
business_overview: Tejas Networks designs and manufactures optical and data networking equipment (routers, switches, 4G/5G RAN gear) sold mainly to Indian telcos and government/PSU customers, notably BSNL's 4G rollout. Tata Sons is the controlling promoter (post its 2022 stake acquisition). Confirmed via screener.in/tickertape as the exact listed entity (NSE: TEJASNET) matching the state.json name. Seeded via untrusted X triage (@nathanit2014 +1, 2026-09-13).
fundamentals_table: Gross debt ~Rs 4,866 Cr; cash ~Rs 589 Cr (Q1 FY27)
fundamentals_narrative: Headline revenue growth (~16% CAGR, ahead of industry) masks a business that is not converting sales into cash or profit: ROCE is deeply negative (-30.56%), ROE has averaged -4% over three years, and debtor days of ~1,077 (nearly three years) point to large, unresolved receivables - consistent with the well-documented delays in BSNL's 4G network payments to its equipment vendors. Gross debt (~Rs 4,866 Cr) dwarfs cash (~Rs 589 Cr), and interest coverage is low. This is a real operating business with genuine India-manufacturing tailwinds, but the P&L and balance sheet do not currently support a positive-return thesis.
technical_read: Trading well off its 52-week high (~Rs 645 vs current levels near/below Rs 550); not pursued further given the fundamentals disposition below.

bull_case: Tata Group-backed (controlling promoter since 2022) with a domestic telecom-equipment manufacturing mandate aligned to India's PLI/Make-in-India push
Revenue CAGR (~16%) ahead of the industry median, indicating real order-book traction (BSNL 4G and other telco/defence contracts)
Optical networking and indigenous 4G/5G RAN gear is a strategically prioritised segment for the Indian government
bear_case: ROCE deeply negative (-30.56%) and ROE negative on a 3-year average - the business is destroying capital at current scale
Debtor days of ~1,077 (nearly 3 years) signal severe working-capital stress, almost certainly tied to delayed government/BSNL payments - a real, unresolved cash-conversion problem
Gross debt (~Rs 4,866 Cr) far exceeds cash (~Rs 589 Cr) with low interest coverage - balance sheet is stretched
Customer concentration risk with government/PSU telecom buyers whose payment cycles are demonstrably unreliable
verdict_headline: Real India-manufacturing tailwind and above-industry revenue growth, but deeply negative ROE/ROCE and an extreme ~1,077-day debtor cycle (government-receivables-driven) mean the numbers don't currently support a thesis fit. four_box = 2.0, thesis_fit 'neither', conviction Low.
